完整生成提示词（本A实际调用）
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: ONE standalone horizontal 16:9 artistic background for a Chinese city cultural webpage; maximum available native clarity, full bleed. Not a webpage screenshot, not a comparison board, no multiple panels.
Creative boundary: original imagined scenes, villagers, artisans, architecture, kites and ordinary craft objects MAY be depicted artistically when they enrich the composition. They are NOT a specific real place, a museum collection object, a historical reconstruction or documentary photography. Clearly illustrated, never presented as evidence. Do not reproduce a particular artist's known work or copy reference imagery. No map or invented administrative boundary.
Background use: compose rich handmade detail away from a naturally quiet reading area, without drawing blank rectangles, cards or UI. Keep a usable calm area within the central vertical mobile-crop strip; exact crop and foreground text will be tested later by the frontend.
No text, characters, calligraphy, inscriptions, signatures, seals, watermarks, logos, QR code, labels, numbers or UI. No photographic rendering, glossy CGI, generic digital wallpaper or smooth synthetic gradients. The only output is the artwork.
A-version medium requirement: Chinese ink painting must be the unmistakable PRIMARY visual language. Show expressive brush pressure, dry-brush flying-white strokes, wet ink blooming into paper, a convincing range from dense black through five ink tones to faint washes, and meaningful empty space. Restrained color ink is allowed. Do NOT substitute watercolor-only mineral puddles, cut-paper outlines, print texture or a shiny material study for ink brushwork. Do not copy a historical painting.
City: Heze. Paint a genuinely freehand Chinese ink peony composition, not a paper-cut flower, textile print, realistic botanical plate or a known historical painting. One powerful but airy branch enters from the UPPER-RIGHT, bends downward along the right edge and releases two loose peony blooms and expressive leaves toward the lower-right. Petals are formed by changing brush pressure, soft wet edges, broken ink, and overlapping pale-grey/pale-lilac washes, with a few dense black leaf strokes and delicate dry stems. Their rhythm must feel spontaneous, varied and alive, not evenly outlined or symmetrical. Leave the LEFT and central-left field broadly open with faint cool paper tone and almost imperceptible washed ink; a little petal mist can reach the bottom of the central phone-crop strip, but its middle remains readable. Palette: black ink, cool pearl-grey, very restrained lavender/mauve ink and almost white paper; no carmine floral wall, no decorative stamp, no antique beige parchment. The cultural cue is the user's Heze peony art context; this is an original imagined floral painting, not an exact local cultivar, actual collection object or specific artist's work. Fine layers of ink value, strong empty-space design and true brush energy. Different orientation and medium from the existing left-heavy red/plum cut-silk B.
